authority: This file is the single definition of Creator OS lane vocabulary. Other documents may reference a lane by id or slug; they may not define, renumber, or redefine one. A prose description that disagrees with this file is stale prose, not a competing definition.
rationale: Three incompatible 'Phase 3' / 'Phase 4' meanings were live at once across docs/creator-os.md, docs/five-intent-program-plan.md, and docs/quest-mission-control.json. A bare ordinal is semantically weak and an agent can execute the wrong work from it. Lanes therefore carry a stable slug as well as an id, and the slug is the safer thing to cite.
citation_rule: Cite a lane as `4A / guild-scale-runtime`, not as `Phase 4`.

work_item_lane_assignment_values.note: The `lane` field on a docs/quest-mission-control.json queue item records a lane ASSIGNMENT. Its value is either a lane id from `lanes` below, or one of the assignment states here. The assignment states are not lanes. They say how a work item stands with respect to lane assignment; they carry no scope, no exit gate, no requirements, and no position in any order of work.
work_item_lane_assignment_values.invariant: An assignment state may never be cited as a lane, appear as a `lane` or `phase` value in docs/creator-requirements-ledger.json, or acquire scheduling semantics. A consumer counting lanes reads `lanes` and nothing else. tools/render_quest_mission_control.py enforces all three: assignment states may not collide with a lane id, a ledger lane or phase must be a lane id, and each assignment state carries its own eligibility rule.
work_item_lane_assignment_values.adding_one: Adding a lane is a sign-off matter. Adding an assignment state is not, because an assignment state cannot schedule anything -- but it must state the condition under which a work item may carry it, or it becomes a way to opt out of the invariant.

assignment_states.meaning: The work item predates this vocabulary, adopted 2026-08-24. It is a historical record, not schedulable work.
assignment_states.rule: Permitted only on a queue item whose state is `complete`, or on a blocked remnant of pre-vocabulary work that carries its own `gated` state.
assignment_states.not: Not a lane, and not `lane 0`. Nothing is scheduled into `pre-lane`; work only ever ends up there by having happened before the vocabulary existed.

assignment_states.meaning: No lane claims this work item, and assigning one would change what a lane covers.
assignment_states.rule: Requires a `lane_note` naming the open question and who must rule on it. This value records a gap; it does not excuse one.
assignment_states.not: Not a lane, and not a readiness state. A queue item may be `ready` and `unassigned` at once -- technically executable, not selected as next work, pending a named ruling. Collapsing that into `blocked` would discard the useful half of it.

human_boundary.allowance: Exactly one human action is permitted per creator session: launching the game and entering the pinned authoring world. Everything after world entry is machine-owned.
human_boundary.strictness_note: The allowance is specifically launch and world entry. It is NOT a generic 'one human intervention' budget. Read as a generic allowance it becomes an escape hatch for any single piece of missing automation, which is precisely the failure it exists to prevent.
not_permitted_under_this_allowance: reading a hash, log, or receipt back to the machine
pressing a key on automation's behalf
verifying any fact the machine can observe
human_boundary.future: Automating world entry is a reduction of this boundary, not a prerequisite for any lane exit. See docs/adr/0012-creator-session-world-entry-is-not-field-lab-orchestration.md.
human_boundary.current_implementation: Installed session queue-full-width-journey-20260827-r9 spent zero human actions: the driver launched Steam into the exact pinned local world, completed the full technical 4A journey, closed Valheim, and restored install, world, and character bytes. ADR 0014 remains the fallback ceiling, not a reason to spend Derek's seat.

not_a_gate_in_any_lane.subject: saved-world packaging
not_a_gate_in_any_lane.detail: Versioned .db/.fwl packaging, inspection, installation, and rollback are not a gate in 4A or 4B. They are owned by lane 5.

lanes.title: Guild-scale runtime
lanes.question: Can Creator OS operate a guild?
in_scope: independent run state for simultaneous experiences
out_of_scope: named anchors, unless the authored slice needs spatial references
general client or server orchestration — bounded exact local-world entry may reduce the human boundary but does not define the 4A exit

acceptance_journey.precondition: One operator owns <Valheim>/BepInEx/ for the lap. NFR-SEAT-003 is satisfied before Derek is called: exact artifacts are installed, every applicable machine step has been driven, evidence and recovery are staged, and mechanical failures have been fixed and rerun.

steps.detail: Drive the real Studio GUI to author and publish one guild pack containing experiences A and B, with B locked behind completion of A.
Attempt B before completing A and retain the fail-closed prerequisite receipt.
Select A, run it to completion, and retain A's first run identity and correlated evidence.
Confirm A's completion unlocks B, then select and advance B under its own run identity.
Select A again and prove the accepted A -> B -> A sequence preserved independent state for both experiences.
Preview and apply a scoped reset to completed experience A only.
Prove B's run identity and progress are unchanged by A's reset.
Rerun A under a new successor run identity linked to the reset and predecessor run.
Use bounded automation to cross the configured per-scope receipt-retention bound by one, then prove both experiences' correlated evidence remains retrievable across live and archived storage.

evidence.detail: Guild, pack, immutable revision, activation, installed content hash, machine, and world identity.
Experience A and B selectors, prerequisite refusal and unlock, independent progress, and B-unchanged-after-A-reset proof.
A's original run, reset, predecessor link, successor run, and B's unaffected run identity.
Accepted and rejected transition/action receipts correlated to activation, experience, run, reset, and world.
Exact receipt bytes remain retrievable across live and archive stores after the per-scope boundary is crossed; no activity in A breaks B's chain.

lanes.exit: Automation drives the real Studio GUI through authoring and publication; proves B refuses before A satisfies its prerequisite; runs the accepted A -> B -> A sequence with independent run state; resets only completed experience A; proves B is unchanged; reruns A under a linked successor identity; crosses the configured receipt-retention boundary; and retains the complete correlated evidence set. The baseline permits at most one human action: launching the game and entering the pinned world. The installed driver defaults to spending zero through bounded exact-world entry. Everything after entry completes without a repository edit, console command, manual file transfer, log read, retry loop, or machine-fact relay.
lanes.failure_mode: The architecture cannot express or execute a guild.

lanes.title: Guild creative systems
lanes.question: Can a steward configure a Guild that creators use to make distinct player experiences over time?
in_scope: steward-owned Guild configuration, bounded palette, and declared progression
one typed creative abstraction instantiated as two meaningfully distinct creator artifacts
one campaign carrying those artifacts through installed Valheim and correlated live evidence
repeated author, validate, play, observe, rerun cycles
proof that the system survives continued use
out_of_scope: new capability that no authored need has demanded
a generic abstraction framework, palette registry, or alternate Runtime artifact format
lanes.exit: One Guild proves the steward -> typed abstraction -> two creator artifacts -> campaign -> installed-player evidence chain; the sustained campaign then covers every declared progression band, every included quest and event has rehearsal evidence, every live-adapter claim has a real run receipt, and multiple author-to-rerun cycles complete without using the seat as process control, input relay, screenshot courier, or machine observer.
lanes.failure_mode: Guild remains a creator-owned pack, the abstraction produces only one disguised copy, or the architecture works once and degrades under sustained use.

lanes.title: Earned acceleration and generation
lanes.question: Which repetitions have earned tooling?
in_scope: generalization only from structures the Guild bridge and campaign actually repeated
optional generation using the same contracts and validators
out_of_scope: anything that becomes required to make a quest
acceleration not traceable to an observed repetition
lanes.exit: Multiple full author-to-rerun cycles complete without a seat turn for machine work; every accepted tooling change links back to an authored need and forward to rerun evidence; and the common loop stays coherent at hundredth-use density.
lanes.failure_mode: Tooling is built for imagined rather than observed need.

lanes.title: Distribution and release
lanes.question: Can someone else receive, inspect, and run what was built?
in_scope: guild release artifact with provenance and dependencies
import, fork lineage, and semantic diff
versioned .db/.fwl world packaging, inspection, installation, and rollback
lanes.exit: Export one guild, import it into a clean local profile, modify it as a fork, inspect the semantic and world diff, install it atomically, and preserve upstream lineage and evidence.
lanes.failure_mode: The work is only runnable on the machine that made it.
